origins: Many people learn this in families where their needs were ignored, mocked, or treated as selfish, or where they had to take care of a parent or siblings. Some were praised for always putting others first, so they learned that having needs was bad. As adults they may say yes to everything, neglect rest and health, and feel resentful or exhausted without knowing why.
teaches: Scripture shows a God who cares about our needs. He opens His hand and satisfies the desires of every living thing, and He promises to supply all our needs in Christ. When Elijah was exhausted and despairing, God gave him food and sleep before anything else. Jesus said to love your neighbor as yourself, which assumes that caring for yourself is normal. Serving others is good, but God never asks you to pretend you have no needs. Your needs matter to Him.
self_statements: Other people’s needs come first, always.
It’s selfish to want anything for myself.
I don’t want to be a bother.
I can rest when everything else is done.
If I say no, people will be upset.
errors: Believing I must either meet every need of others or be selfish.
Telling myself I should never need anything.
Ignoring the times my needs were met and it was good.
Assuming others will be upset if I express a need.
questions: Where did I learn that my needs don’t matter?
What needs am I ignoring right now?
Is caring for myself really selfish?
How did God care for Elijah when he was exhausted?
What happens to me when I ignore my needs for too long?
What is one need I could honestly express this week?
truth: I care about others, and that is good. But my needs matter too, to God and to the people who love me. God supplies my needs and cares about my body, rest, and feelings. I can take care of myself and still serve others.
hw_truths: God will supply all my needs.
Rest and care are not selfish.
I can love others as I love myself.
log: Each day, write one need you noticed in yourself and what you did about it.
actions: Write a list of what you need: rest, food, friendship, quiet, help. Circle one to address this week.
Decline one request this week that you would normally accept out of guilt. Notice what happens.
Put one hour of rest or enjoyment on your calendar and keep it like an appointment.
Tell one trusted person about a need you have, and let them help.
tracker: A need I took care of
prayer: Father, I have treated my needs as unimportant for so long. Thank You that You care about all of me and promise to supply what I need. Teach me to rest, to speak up, and to receive care without guilt. Amen.
meta: Christian belief counseling for “My needs don’t matter.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
